text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger, including when it started and if you have noticed any redness or warmth. Also, have you recently experienced a puncture wound to that finger, such as from a thorn or nail?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: The mechanism of injury sounds suspicious for a plantar flexion injury or a deep laceration, which can lead to a foreign body infection like a felon or septic arthritis. Given the progressive nature over two days, have you noticed any pus drainage, severe throbbing pain when the finger is held in a specific position, or any limitation in your ability to straighten or bend the finger? speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Flexor Digitorum Superficialis (FDS) Tendon Rupture. The mechanism of injury (finger caught and pulled) combined with the specific finding of the inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint confirms a rupture of the FDS tendon.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
